newsitem.title: USA: Dallas panel mulls municipal disclosure regs.
newsitem.headline: Dallas panel mulls municipal disclosure regs.

text.p: While some Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure rules are easily met, others are challenging or cloudy enough to merit concern, voices from various corners of the municipal market said during a conference.

"This is a new world for all of us, and we are kind of tiptoeing into it and trying to figure out what we are supposed to be doing," Richard Porter, a partner at the Texas law firm of McCall Parkhurst & Horton LLP, said on a panel during the Bond Buyer's second annual Texas Public Finance Conference on Tuesday.
Porter was involved in an informal inquiry by the SEC regarding of his clients, he said, adding that "luckily, that one came out nicely." Porter also learned a lot, he said.
One lesson was the value of hiring an attorney experienced in securities litigation. Both he and the general counsel involved recommended that the issuer hire such an attorney, he said.
"It is important, I believe, to fully cooperate with the SEC's inquiries, but I believe you must do so using the resources of a person who is experienced in dealing in this area," Porter said.

John Roan, assistant vice chancellor for finance at the University of Texas System, said the system's experience with the new rules so far has been with preparation of official statements and the annual update, both of which have "gone very smoothly."

"We don't have any problems in deciding what goes in and what doesn't go in," he said. The issuer's staff remains concerned, however, about how to maintain uniform disclosure of material events and information that crops up during the year.

"We are a diverse system," Roan said. "We have 15 institutions with substantial public exposure in their local market areas." For instance, in Dallas the university system has a research laboratory associated with Southwestern Medical Center, which is involved in cancer research among other areas, and which could potentially generate some postitive news, he said. "What about all those times during the year when things happen at one or more of our 15 institutions, good and bad? How do we collect that information, assess it from a materiality standpoint, and when do we make disclosure of that? I think we are grappling with that right now," Roan said.

The system has at least four locations in which a local investment market could act quickly on press reports confined to a specific area, gaining an advantage in market transactions, he said. Roan added that the system does not want continually disclose issues it believes will make no difference to bond buyers and sellers.
One area needing clarification is whether a substantial financial improvement in a triple-A credit warrants reporting.
"You are already rated AAA, does it mean anything for you to make disclosure on something like that?" Roan asked.
Barry Smitherman, Texas office manager and a vice president of public finance at JP Morgan Securities Inc, represented the broker-dealers' perspective on the panel.

"Obviously we support disclosure, and we support efforts to promote greater disclosure," Smitherman said, adding that JP Morgan's public finance client base, for the most part, consists of large and sophisticated issuers like the University of Texas.
Such issuers are frequently in the market and provide comprehensive annual reports and other information to investors, making the kinds of material disclosures that are desired, he said.
"Nevertheless, in the case of primary market disclosure I must say that there is an increasing nervousness that firms like ours may be viewed as disclosure guarantors," Smitherman said.

"One approach a firm can take to try to obviate this concern is to try to get indemnification from the issuer, but as you know in Texas and some other jurisdications, that's problematic." From JP Morgan's perspective, the best solution is to "choose your clients carefully," Smitherman said.
"As I said, we choose to do business with the University of Texas, we choose not to do business with a number of other public entities," he said.
